experiment.title: Ares Alpha
experiment.hypothesis: A Mars settlement becomes civilization-like when material resilience, technological capacity, citizen specialization, collective decision quality, and historical memory reinforce one another over time.

significant_events.title: Citizen Nora Jensen proposed an operational upgrade.

success_signals.signal: The colony remains viable through the full observation window without deterministic collapse.
Citizens develop differentiated histories instead of remaining interchangeable records.
Major events leave measurable traces in both state and memory.
The colony can recover from at least some adverse events rather than only decline.
The chronicle explains meaningful state changes in human-readable form.

failure_signals.signal: Resource collapse is mathematically inevitable under healthy initial conditions.
Population changes occur without causal events or explanation.
Citizen professions do not materially affect outcomes.
History diverges from actual simulation state.
Repeated runs with the same seed produce inconsistent outcomes without an explicit source of nondeterminism.

report.insight: Ares Alpha remained viable across the observation window with a resource floor of 79.10; technology changed by 65.11 and CQ by 0.58, supporting the hypothesis that material resilience and coordinated capability can reinforce one another.
